Meeting header:
Date: 2026-04-11 15:30 PDT
Duration: 62 minutes
Meeting ID: ff-2026-04-11-halcyon-bridging-trust-01
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Liam (Redwood SE), Zara (Redwood CSM), Diego (Redwood Reliability), Priya (Halcyon Head AI Ops), Marcus (Halcyon VP Eng), Jasmine (Halcyon SRE), Ethan (Halcyon Procurement)

Optional auto sections (generated):
Summary: Quick post-incident sync to walk through what happened during the 2026-04-09 platform degradation, align on root cause evidence, agree on stop-gap mitigations and long-term reliability / SLA changes, and set concrete next steps to restore customer trust.

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining on short notice. I'm Maya Patel from Redwood, AE on the Halcyon account — appreciate you all making time. The goal today is to be candid: walk through what we know, what we don't, and concrete remedial steps.
[00:24] Priya: Thanks Maya. We got a lot of internal questions — executives want plain answers. There was a customer-facing outage window and while we had fallbacks, machine-learning responses were delayed and some jobs returned errors. We want to understand whether this was a single point in your infra or something with how we use the KV cache.
[00:40] Liam: Yep, hi — Liam O'Connor, Redwood SE. I'll start with the short timeline from our side. On 04-09 at ~02:14 UTC we saw an abrupt spike in request volume for Halcyon that exceeded the autoscaler threshold and coincided with concurrent prefix cache evictions. That created amplified tail latency plus some OOM retries on a small subset of dedicated workers. We briefly lost the hot-KV window which caused rehydration churn.
[01:05] Jasmine: There were also retries from our side — our client retried on 500s which made the burst worse. We have the retry policy logs and can share. Some of our ops people noticed a high p95 but it didn't fully surface to the apps until downstream timeouts.
[01:28] Marcus: Quick question — were we on Dedicated or Hosted at the time? I thought we were on Dedicated pool with reserved capacity.
[01:35] Diego: You are on Dedicated, but the autoscaler + fallback path still talks to a secondary pool for overflow. The overflow routing was engaged after the first pool's session limits were hit. The overflow pool had slightly higher cold-start latency.
[01:52] Priya: So is the core issue routing or the actual model worker instability? We saw error patterns that look like KV mismatch but also increased GC on the worker pods.
[02:06] Liam: It's a blend — primary issue was unanticipated traffic amplification combined with aggressive prefix eviction. The eviction logic kicked in because the sequence of long context requests grew the in-memory cache beyond the tuned working set; then we observed rehydration thundering. There's also a smaller contributor: a kernel regression in our runtime that increases mem fragmentation for a rare sequence pattern. We're tracking that with the runtime team.
[02:37] Marcus: Kernel regression? Can you be more concrete — is that a Redwood runtime patch you can roll back?
[02:43] Liam: Yes, it's a revision rolled out in late March that changes memory allocator heuristics for quantized op paths. We can roll forward with a mitigation flag to reduce fragmentation or roll back the revision; both are possible but we need to weigh risk.
[02:57] Priya: We need timelines — the execs asked whether this is something that could happen again if we see another traffic surge.
[03:05] Maya: Short answer: unlikely with mitigations, but not zero. Over next 72 hours we plan to: 1) disable the new allocator heuristic for Halcyon's Dedicated pool to reduce mem fragmentation; 2) apply a safer KV eviction policy (increase working-set threshold) to avoid premature evictions; 3) run a controlled replay of Halcyon's traffic to validate rehydration behavior.
[03:28] Ethan: From procurement/legal — will any of this change the contract or require credits? We had SLA clauses for availability.
[03:36] Zara: We'll surface a formal RCA and also the impact math to inform credits. That will be part of the follow-up deck. Today's sync is to agree root cause and plan.
[03:48] Marcus: I want to drill into the autoscaler config — our ops team tuned aggressive scale-up because we care about latency. If the autoscaler overshoots and evictions happen, we get this cascade. Can we get the actual autoscaler graphs and thresholds?
[04:05] Liam: Absolutely — we'll export the scaling traces, pod lifecycle events, and eviction markers. We'll also flag which nodes fell into OOM-kill.
[04:15] Jasmine: Also, some of our logs show KV cache entries with mismatched keys after rehydration, like some key prefixes were missing — could this be a serialization mismatch?
[04:27] Diego: There's a note — during the rehydrate churn some of the cache metadata update path had a race condition under high concurrency. Our observation is metadata writes lagged behind reads for a short window; that manifests as transient missing prefixes. That's a code-path fix we have a patch for.
[04:47] Priya: Ok. Are these two separate things then — the runtime allocator and the KV metadata race? Which is the dominant cause?
[04:56] Liam: Root cause is the interplay: allocator regression made memory pressure worse during rehydration, which increased eviction frequency; evictions triggered rehydration which exposed the metadata race and caused some requests to fail rather than be served by fallback. Dominant root cause: traffic amplification + allocator regression. Secondary: KV metadata race.
[05:16] Marcus: Can you share the patch timeline for both?
[05:20] Diego: For the metadata race we have a hotfix candidate that can be deployed within 48 hours to Dedicated pools. For allocator changes we can either flip a runtime flag immediately (minutes) to revert to the previous behavior, or schedule a more thorough rollback validated in canary over 5 days. Recommendation: do the runtime flag flip as immediate mitigation, deploy metadata hotfix in 48 hours, then run a replay.
[05:42] Priya: That sounds reasonable. What about longer-term — will you change eviction heuristics permanently?
[05:48] Liam: We'll propose different eviction profiles per workload type: Halcyon is heavy-context retail conversational, so we should give it a higher working-set threshold. We'll suggest a profile change and run perf tests.
[05:58] Marcus: Any signal we should surface in our monitoring to catch this earlier?
[06:01] Jasmine: Yes, page on sustained rehydrate rate > X/min plus p95 tail shift > Yms. Also detect sudden drop in cache hit rate alongside rising request rate.
[06:12] Maya: We'll also add explicit alerts for eviction storms and link them to the incident runbook so ops gets immediate remediation steps (e.g., temporarily disable aggressive retries, route to secondary read-only cached variant).
[06:27] Priya: On the customer side we had questions about data integrity — were any inference results persisted to our downstream store incorrectly?
[06:36] Diego: From our audit, we didn't see successful writes of corrupted inference outputs to long-term stores. There were some partial responses cached in-memory but those did not reach persistence layer. Still, we'll run an integrity sweep.
[06:50] Priya: Ok, that's huge — we'll need that as written evidence.
[06:55] Marcus: About SLAs — do you have a precedent for credits in cases where the failure is due to a runtime regression?
[07:05] Zara: We handle on a case-by-case basis; we'll include impact math with the RCA and then propose remediations plus a credits offer consistent with our SLA.
[07:14] Ethan: Procurement will need the formal RCA and the list of mitigations before moving forward on the renewal timeline.
[07:20] Maya: Understood. We'll deliver the RCA, timeline, and proposed SLA adjustments.
[07:26] [09:03] Speaker 2: (crosstalk) just to add, there was a surge from a third-party vendor that coincided with your internal load test, not sure which triggered it first.
[09:12] Priya: That's important — we did run a release test at ~02:10 UTC, but not an intended full-scale load. We'll correlate schedules.
[09:20] Liam: We'll ingest your release test log and overlay it on our traffic traces.
[09:34] [12:00] Priya: Two practical asks: 1) we need a step-by-step rollback playbook for the event, 2) a lab test that simulates our peak behavior that we can run jointly.
[12:10] Diego: We'll produce a rollback playbook (runbook) with checklist: disable runtime flag, increase eviction threshold, scale policy to X, route overflow to read-only variant, and monitor cache hit rate. We'll also run a joint replay in our staging environment with synthetic traffic to validate.
[12:36] Maya: For the joint replay, we'll need a scrubbed request sample set from Halcyon. Priya, can you provide an anonymized sample of the request distribution?
[12:45] Priya: Yes, we'll coordinate with SRE to send a scrubbed set.
[12:50] Marcus: On the exec messaging front, we want a short one-page timeline and the top three mitigations.
[12:58] Maya: We'll provide that.
[13:05] Jasmine: Quick note — in our customer-facing logs we saw a few malformed tokenization exceptions that might be from a different model variant. Could be unrelated but we'll flag it.
[13:16] Liam: Noted — we'll correlate model variants and tokenizer versions; sometimes mismatch can happen after rollout if the model revision metadata isn't pinned.
[13:30] Priya: We also want clarity on observability retention — some traces we needed were truncated at 7 days and we had to escalate to support. Can we increase retention for Halcyon for 30 days while we finish the RCA?
[13:42] Zara: We can temporarily increase tracing retention for the account; we'll include the cost estimate in the follow-up.
[13:49] Ethan: Cost estimate needed for finance approval.
[13:52] Maya: We'll include both the retention cost and the potential credits in the deck.
[14:00] Marcus: Another ask: in future, can Redwood surface an early-warning dashboard for our stakeholders, something non-technical that shows service health and expected delivery timelines?
[14:10] Zara: Yes, we have a lightweight incident status page we can enable per account; we'll turn that on and give you a URL.
[14:20] Priya: Great.
[14:30] Liam: Back to technicals: we'll run three experiments for validation — (A) runtime flag revert on a canary host; (B) metadata race hotfix on a small subset; (C) eviction profile change and stress test. Each experiment has success criteria: keep p95 < target and avoid cache miss spike > threshold.
[14:58] Marcus: Success criteria need to be measurable, put numbers in the deck.
[15:05] Maya: We'll include them.
[15:10] Jasmine: For runbook steps, include an emergency fallback: route traffic to a smaller lower-latency model that is read-only and serves cached answers until workers stabilize.
[15:22] Liam: That fallback exists and we'll document the latency delta.
[15:28] Priya: Any legal/regulatory implications? We process EU resident PII for some users; was any data exposed?
[15:36] Diego: No evidence of data exfiltration. The incident was an availability event; we'll include our audit logs and KMS access logs to prove no unauthorized access.
[15:48] Priya: Please ensure those logs are timestamped and signed so our compliance team can validate.
[15:54] Maya: We'll deliver signed audit artifacts.
[16:01] [End of main discussion, final 7 min recap]
[16:02] Maya: Recap — agreed mitigation plan: immediate runtime flag flip, metadata hotfix in 48 hours, eviction profile change and joint replay. Deliverables: RCA deck and raw logs (by 2026-04-12), runbook and remediation playbook (by 2026-04-15), temporary trace retention and incident status page. Action owners listed in the follow-up.
[16:25] Priya: Good. For transparency we need the exact list of nodes and the log slices that show the OOMs and eviction spikes.
[16:33] Diego: We'll export node-level events and point to the exact times.
[16:36] Marcus: After the deck, let's schedule the SLA renegotiation review — 30 minutes with Halcyon execs.
[16:42] Ethan: Procurement will be on that call.
[16:45] Maya: I'll coordinate dates via email.
[16:49] Priya: Anything else?
[16:52] Jasmine: One more: confirm whether model quantization settings changed recently — we had a note that a quantized variant was rolled to Dedicated in late March.
[16:59] Liam: It was part of the March revision; quantization settings are tied to the runtime change we discussed. We'll include exact model variant IDs in the deck.
[17:08] Maya: Thanks everyone. We'll follow up with the RCA and the playbook; Zara will open the incident timeline doc and keep it updated.
[17:16] [Meeting closed]
